title: replay-driven-performance-investigation-diary
summary: Working notes for a replay-driven approach used to reproduce a performance regression that surfaced in hosted canaries. Includes checklist, PromQL queries to validate, replayer run recipes, bisect guidance, and artifacts to collect for handoff.
body:
Context and goal:
- Incident: p95 tail latency drift noticed in hosted canary between 2025-02-18 02:00 UTC and 2025-02-18 03:30 UTC (SLO breach on short bursts).
- Hypothesis: regression introduced in runtime scheduling or a kernel selection change interacting badly with seq_len > 512 requests under bursty arrival patterns.
- Goal: reproducibly replay the canary window, isolate the commit range, and produce concrete artifacts (profiles, heap/kv cache stats, kernel timings) for a rollback or patch.

Quick notes about the dataset and approach:
- We used the archived request trace from canary-run-2025-02-18-02 (s3://redwood-prod-perf/canaries/canary-2025-02-18-02.trace.gz).
- Trace contains ~62k requests, 92% text-generation, median seq_len=180, 12% seq_len>512.
- Replayer options tuned to preserve arrival pattern and jitter: --preserve-interarrival --jitter=0.05 --max-concurrency=600 (target concurrency to match observed in prod).
- Replay is best-effort; to match GPU scheduling, we pin the replayer to same instance types (g5.12xlarge equivalent) and the same runtime image sha (serving-runtime:sha-2025-02-09).

Steps taken (chronological):
1) Snapshot ingestion:
   - pulled trace and metadata, validated checksums.
   - extracted request histogram and session grouping (user_id hashed) to preserve locality.
2) Baseline golden run (pre-regression):
   - replayer run against known-good image (serving-runtime:sha-2025-01-28).
   - collect: per-request token timing, host-level perf counters (nvidia-smi sampling + nvprof micro traces), and Prometheus scrape of runtime/exporter at 10s.
   - observed p95: 128ms, p99: 320ms for seq_len<=512; seq_len>512 p95: 410ms.
3) Suspect run (post-regression):
   - run same trace against candidate image (serving-runtime:sha-2025-02-06).
   - observed p95: 149ms (+16%), seq_len>512 p95: 488ms (+19%). CPU steal events and elevated kernel spin observed.
4) Narrowing the window with git-bisect:
   - marked good at 2025-01-28 commit, bad at 2025-02-06.
   - automated bisect pipeline: checkout -> build container -> run small representative sample (10k reqs, same distribution) -> capture p95.
   - halting criteria: >10% increase in p95 on sample or obvious kernel-time spike in perf.
   - bisect found potential offending commit range: 2025-02-02 -> 2025-02-04 (3 commits touching allocator and kernel selection).

Investigation heuristics & what we looked at:
- Token-level timing breakdown: prefix decode, attention-kv, matmul, softmax, memory-copy. Compare relative shares across runs.
- Kernel-selection logs: enable verbose kernel debug (RUNTIME_KERNEL_DEBUG=1) to see chosen cuBLAS/cutlass or fallback path.
- NVTX ranges around the attention and matmul to correlate GPU traces with high-level phases.
- Host-level counters: context-switches, softirq, irq, page faults (minor/major), CPU cpuset pinning failures.
- Cache hit ratio (KV cache) during replay. If prefetching behavior changed, cache churn can amplify tail latency.

PromQL snippets used for quick dashboards:
- p95 latency for model route:
  - histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))
- kernel selection failures (custom metric):
  - sum(rate(runtime_kernel_selection_errors_total[5m])) by (instance)
- GPU utilization and scaling windows:
  - max_over_time(gpu_utilization[1m])

Replayer recipe (commands we used):
- docker run --rm -e RUNTIME_KERNEL_DEBUG=1 -e REPLAYER_PRESERVE_INTERARRIVAL=1 \
  -v /tmp/trace:/trace redwood/serving-runtime:sha-YYYY run-replay --trace /trace/canary-2025-02-18.trace --concurrency 600 --jitter 0.05 --output /trace/out.json
- After run: python tools/aggregate_trace.py /trace/out.json --emit-profiles /trace/profiles/

Artifacts to collect (canonical list for incident handoff):
- Replayer raw output (out.json) + aggregated summary.csv
- nvprof/nvtx GPU ranges (.nvprof or .qdrep), and translated timeline into speedscope-friendly JSON
- perf or linux perf script output for host-side syscall breakdown (perf.data)
- Prometheus export snapshot covering the run and a 20m window before/after
- Container logs, especially runtime debug logs with magic markers around kernel selection
- Git SHAs for runtime and build metadata (compiler flags, CUDA driver version, cuBLAS/cuDNN build ids)

Findings so far (non-conclusive but actionable):
- Kernel-path divergence: suspect commit introduced an extra fallback path for small-matrix matmul that was frequently chosen for attention slices with dim<=64. The fallback increases matmul time by ~22% for those slices and seems to affect bursts where many small matmuls are scheduled concurrently.
- Host noise: during the bad replay runs, we observed a small but measurable increase in irq and softirq counts, possibly due to a side-effect of a driver upgrade in the image.
- KV cache churn: slight increase in cache eviction rate on bad run (evictions +7%), likely due to changed prefetch order in the scheduler.

Immediate mitigations tried:
- Roll forward to keep kernel selection conservative (force use of old matmul path) via env override: RUNTIME_FORCE_MATMUL_PATH="cutlass_v1". This reduced p95 on bad image to within 5% of baseline for sampled replay.
- Temporarily increase canary abort sensitivity: reduce canary thresholds for tail latency and enable immediate rollback on repeated SLO breaches.

Open questions / next steps:
- Do we have enough signal to pin the regression solely to the matmul fallback? Need a focused microbenchmark across various matrix dims and batch sizes with/without the new selector.
- Driver/OS upgrade link: correlate image component diffs between the two SHAs (list kernel modules, NVIDIA driver versions).
- Check interplay between prefetch scheduler and KV cache eviction: instrument scheduler to emit prefetch order traces.

Checklist before sign-off to product and SRE:
- [ ] Reproduce regression on identical instance type using replay (done for 3 runs, need two more for statistical confidence).
- [ ] Produce microbenchmark results that isolate matmul path performance delta (include raw timings).
- [ ] Prepare rollback PR / hotfix with env override and add unit/regression test that covers small-matmul heavy workloads.
- [ ] Postmortem draft with timeline, root cause, and action items (link to SERV-3421).

Notes to reviewers:
- The replayer is a fidelity approximation; small differences vs. live may remain (kernel scheduling, tenant noise). Treat replay as strong evidence but pair with prod-side sampling to close the loop.
- If you run replayer locally, be sure to use the same driver stack as listed in linked_artifacts to avoid false negatives.

Appendix: quick reproduction commands and small benchmarks to run locally:
- small-matmul microbench (python snippet):
  - python benchmarks/matmul_sweep.py --dims 8 16 32 64 128 --backend cuda --iters 2000 --out /tmp/matmul.csv
- sample PromQL to compare baseline vs candidate during replay windows (use grafana Explore):
  - compare: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{instance=~"replay.*"}[1m])) by (le))

Contact for follow-ups: Asha Patel (owner), cc: Jordan Kim, Diego Morales, Priya Singh.

End of diary entry for the 2025-02-18 canary replay. More notes will be appended here as further microbenchmarks and bisect results land.
